title: Understand Equations and Their Solutions
objective: I can write an equation for a real situation and check whether a given value is a solution by substituting it.
model: balance scale and word clue: write the equation from the story, then substitute a value and see whether both pans balance

widgets.component: evaluate 4n at n = 6 and 30 − k at k = 12; 'a number increased by 7'; what the equal sign says
widgets.root: Prerequisite review (evaluate an expression, the equal sign as 'same value'); keys 24, n + 7, 'both sides have the same value', 18 verified. The lesson's own warm-up is on reflections (7-9), so this section replaces it with the right prerequisite.

widgets.component: write the equation for 'a number plus 12 equals 30', 'seven less than', 'three times', 'divided by 4'; is n = 3 a solution of n + 5 = 9; '8 − n = 5' error
widgets.root: Translation keys n + 12 = 30, n − 7 = 18, 3n = 21, n / 4 = 8 and the substitution (3 + 5 = 8, not 9) verified; the error flags the written equation (e=2), the first wrong step.

widgets.component: fingerprints f + 14 = 30; cameras c + 6 = 19; 'divided by 3' written as 3n
widgets.root: Keys f + 14 = 30 and c + 6 = 19 right; error step e=2 is the first wrong step.

widgets.component: generated: is w = 21 a solution of w − 12 = 11, which value of d makes d + 7 = 15 true, complete the equation so t = 15 is a solution
widgets.root: L1-L3 are only substitute-and-compare (choice with the arithmetic shown, 'which value makes it true' from four candidates, or complete the right side). Evaluated 1,004 generated draws across L1-L4 (300 seeds each) by substituting into both sides: 0 wrong keys, exactly one true candidate in every 'which value/equation' item; no inverse-operation step is needed.

widgets.where: Practice 4.7; Challenge 3.1-3.2 (act:balance form check L2, L3, L4)
widgets.component: put each candidate number in the bag and see whether the scale balances
widgets.root: Real model of 'solution = both pans equal': the left pan is computed for each candidate and the heavier pan goes down; candidates include the reversed-operation and unchanged-total distractors. L3-L4 add multiplication, decimals and fractions.

widgets.component: 'Solve p + 14 = 37', 'Why subtract 14 from BOTH sides?', 'Check your answer: does 23 work?'
widgets.root: Solving by subtracting the same number from both sides and the reason (keep the equation balanced while isolating p) is the objective, worked example, vocabulary (Isolate, Inverse operation, Subtraction Property of Equality) and Learn It of 8-2, whose first worked example is n + 23 = 58 solved this way. 8-1's objective is to write the equation and test a given value by substituting. The three items come from 8-1's own Connect check (config connect.check[0]), so the drift is in the canonical lesson too. 5.3 also depends on 5.1's answer ('does 23 work?') and names no equation.
widgets.replacement: Replace 5.1-5.3 with substitution only: 5.1 'Is p = 23 a solution of p + 14 = 37? Substitute and decide' (choices show 23 + 14 = 37; 23 − 14 = 9; 37 − 14 = 23; 14 + 37 = 51); 5.2 an act:balance {form:'check'} or a three-row table (p = 14, 23, 51: left side, right side, solution yes/no); 5.3 an error item 'Rana says p = 51 because 37 + 14 = 51. Find the step where substituting shows she is wrong.' Remove the 'subtract from both sides' item entirely (8-2). Keep the equation in every stem.

widgets.component: which value is the solution of n + 5 = 9; which r is a solution of r + 15 = 40
widgets.root: Keys n = 4 (4 + 5 = 9) and r = 25 verified; both are substitution questions with named traps ('5 appears in the equation', 'close to 4').

widgets.component: is x = 27 a solution of x ÷ 9 = 5; 34 = x + 12; which value makes 11 = x ÷ 9 true
widgets.root: Substitution with the arithmetic shown in the choices; keys recomputed over 300 seeds.

widgets.component: 'Which equation has d = 17 as its solution', story solution checks, and 'One number makes both equations true: b + 3 = 17 and 42 = 3b. What is the number?'
widgets.root: 74 of 300 L4 draws (25%) are the typed-answer 'one number makes both equations true' form. With no candidates to test, the student has to solve b + 3 = 17 by subtracting and 42 = 3b by dividing, which are 8-2 and 8-3 methods; the rest of L4 (which equation has this solution, is 7.3 a solution of 9w = 56.7) is substitution and fine.
widgets.replacement: Remove the 'both equations true' variant from solutionCheck L4 or turn it into a choice item ('Which value makes both equations true? 8, 14, 17, 20') so it is solved by testing; leave 'which equation has n as its solution' and 'is w = 7.3 a solution of 9w = 56.7'.

widgets.component: 'twice a number is n + 2' error; write a story for n / 5 = 9; playlist 18 + t = 45 on a tape diagram; test 3m = 42 table; whole number t with 2t = 26 between 10 and 15; stickers s − 9 = 15
widgets.root: Table rows 30/12, 42/0, 54/12, 36/6 and 13, t = 27, s = 24 recomputed; the tape diagram splits 45 into 18 and t; 2.5 is guess-and-bound by bracketing, not inverse operations.

widgets.component: sort six equations by whether x = 6 is a solution; three error analyses (8 − n, 'close to 10', 45 for 4c); Amara/Dev; microphones m − 6 = 11; 7y = 56; n = 12; count of w = 14 solutions; write-your-own story
widgets.root: Sort bins (x + 9 = 15, 4x = 24, x ÷ 2 = 3 yes; x ÷ 3 = 18, 7x = 49, x − 2 = 8 no) and error steps (e=2, 2, 1) verified; keys m − 6 = 11, y = 8, n ÷ 4 = 3 and 3 equations (14 + 5, 14 − 5, 5 × 14 = 70 yes; 14 ÷ 2 = 28 no) are right.

widgets.component: 'A value p makes p ÷ 4 = 9 true. What is p?'
widgets.root: No candidates are offered, so the student solves a division equation; the item's hint ('Multiplication undoes division') and wrong-answer feedback ('to undo a division, use the opposite operation') teach the 8-3 inverse-operation method inside 8-1.
widgets.replacement: Make it a substitution item: 'Which value of p makes p ÷ 4 = 9 true?' with choices 5, 13, 36, 2.25 (the four traps already written), or give p = 36 and ask the student to show the division that proves it. Delete the inverse-operation hint and feedback.

formulaOrder.formula: x + a = b → x = b − a (subtract the same number from both sides)
x ÷ a = b → x = a × b (multiplication undoes division)

typography: Division is printed 'n / 12 = 30', 'n / 4 = 8' in Practice 2.1-2.3, 2.5, 3.1, 3.3 (choices), 3.2 (steps) and Challenge 2.2 (stem), 5.6 (frame), while the generated items, the balance scale and Challenge 3.3, 4.4, 5.2, 5.4 print '÷'; one studio uses two division symbols, and '/' reads as a fraction bar.
